related_questions.question: What are the requirements to fly to Portugal?

text_blocks.snippet: To fly to Portugal, you generally need a passport that is valid for at least three months beyond your intended stay. Depending on your nationality, you might also need a visa for stays longer than 90 days within the Schengen area. As of now, no COVID-19 related restrictions apply for entry into Portugal.
snippet_highlighted_words: a passport that is valid for at least three months beyond your intended stay

list.title: Validity:
list.snippet: Your passport must be valid for at least three months beyond your intended departure date from the Schengen area.

list.title: Blank Pages:
list.snippet: You should have at least two blank pages in your passport for entry and exit stamps.

list.title: Exceptions:
list.snippet: EU citizens, and those from Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland, can enter with a valid national ID card.

list.title: Schengen Area:
list.snippet: Portugal is part of the Schengen area, which allows for stays of up to 90 days within a 180-day period without a visa for citizens of certain countries.

list.title: Visa Required:
list.snippet: If you are not from a visa-exempt country or plan to stay longer than 90 days, you will need to apply for a Schengen visa.

list.title: ETIAS:
list.snippet: Starting in 2025, travelers from visa-exempt countries will need to apply for ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorization System) authorization before traveling.

list.title: Return Ticket:
list.snippet: While not mandatory, it's advisable to have a return ticket or proof of sufficient funds to cover your return.

list.title: Proof of Funds:
list.snippet: You may be asked to demonstrate you have sufficient funds to support yourself during your stay.

list.title: COVID-19:
list.snippet: As of now, Portugal does not require proof of vaccination or a negative COVID-19 test for entry, according to Portugal.com.
